analysis:
The only content change in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md is the added paragraph at head lines 757-765. It documents streamed `auto` tool-call chunking: the first chunk carries id, type, name and empty arguments, later chunks carry only index and argument fragments, and consumers concatenate by index. This is documentation only and changes no wire message shape, encryption, attestation, authorization or custody behavior. It sits under `inference_response_chunk`, which already carries `encrypted_data` for E2E encryption, so the threat model for T-008 (fail-closed encryption) is unaffected by this text. The rest of the head text in units 9-11 is unchanged context, and I found nothing in it that contradicts the threat model.

The real code change is the submodule pointer bump of libs/mlx-swift-lm from 889fe3cc to 118ffb0a. The submodule contents were not supplied, so I cannot review them. The doc cites `MLXOpenAIService.streamChatCompletionFrames` as the source of the new chunking behavior, so the update likely touches the streaming and tool-call path inside the provider's inference engine (TB-007). Possible concerns for the next pass are whether streamed tool-call fragments still pass through the same encryption path (T-008), whether tool-call parsing or constraint handling alters reserved-schema-metadata rejection, and whether the engine, prefix-cache (T-041) or KV code was touched. None of this is verifiable here. I report no finding because there is no visible evidence of a regression, but the unreviewed submodule diff is a coverage gap, so I set needs_deeper_review=true.
